result.title: Separation of Skilling Context for Standard Operating Procedure-based Agents
result.summary: Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) are kept concise for human readability, so LLM agents that generate executable skills from them lack the tacit knowledge and implementation details needed for automation. Human intervention fills these gaps, but must be repeated as SOPs evolve---a problem we call \textit{SOP-skill drift}. We propose managing SOPs and Contextual Knowledge (CK) separately, together with a \textit{contract-aware} evaluation that distinguishes genuine violations from CK-resolved differences. On eight Indeed-derived workflows (single LLM), it raises the functional-equivalence rate from 12\% to 58\%. Under three SOP-revision perturbations, previously extracted CK already covers 79.5\% of newly introduced automation gaps.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究从简洁 SOP 生成可执行 skill 时的隐性知识缺口，提出将 SOP 与 Contextual Knowledge 分开管理，并用 contract-aware 评测区分真实违规与知识补全后的差异。
AI.relevance_reason: 该工作面向 SOP 驱动的 agent skill 生成与流程演化，未涉及视觉推理状态、证据使用或 latent 表示；其知识分离与评测思路与 LVR 主线缺少具体可核查的方法联系。
